title: Empirical detection of influential coordinates
statement: Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer and let $f:\{−1,1\}^n\to\{−1,1\}$ be monotone. Let $t\in\mathbb Q$ be positive and let $\varepsilon\in\mathbb Q$ satisfy $0<\varepsilon\le 1/2$; suppose the total influence of the real-valued sign version of $f$ is at most $t$. For each singleton Fourier query, take the prescribed sample of inputs, and suppose its empirical Fourier coefficient differs from the true coefficient by less than the prescribed accuracy. Then every coordinate whose Boolean influence is at least the prescribed learning threshold belongs to the empirical set of influential coordinates formed from these samples.
hypotheses_covered: The target is a Boolean function on the sign cube of dimension $n$
The influence bound $t$ is a positive rational
The learning parameter $\varepsilon$ is rational with $0<\varepsilon\le1/2$
Total influence of the real-valued sign version is at most $t$
For every singleton Fourier query, the sample avoids its coefficient bad set, equivalently the empirical coefficient error is strictly below the prescribed accuracy
